notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every value (the four users' names, emails, phones, roles and active flags; the group at GROUP_009 with its name, type, description, active = 1 and Neha as manager resolved by email) and on all three dispositions (kept). disagreement: form: the group's manager: A a separate requirement, B folded into the group's cells; kept A's split (logged in the group requirement). disagreement: form: the memberships: A one set requirement counting distinct members, B one requirement per member; kept B's per-row form (logged in Arjun's membership requirement). disagreement: stay that the four do not join GROUP_003 or GROUP_004, the seed's two existing 'Service Desk' groups (A only); dropped because the membership requirements already select the new group GROUP_009, so a run that adds the four to an existing Service Desk group instead fails them and the benchmark's membership check without the stay, and the request does not forbid other memberships (collateral changes are measured separately). Seed facts re-checked at merge: no seed user has a company.com email, one of the four names or a +91-98101 phone; GROUP_008 is the highest group and USER_100 the highest user; the acting user USER_039 is an admin. The users table carries role and active directly (the benchmark check reads users.role); the user_role table is not tested because neither the request nor the policy fixes it. The policy (sha 9aa56c2a) says nothing about user creation, future start dates or group managers, so the active flags for the two future joiners rest on the benchmark check plus the request's 'joining fifteen days from now'. revised: the form disagreement on the memberships now states its own reason (several rows created in one table are each selected by their own natural key) in place of a reference to a form convention.
